Subject: Request: Dedicated capacity review for production (throughput & latency)

Hi Sofia,

We just completed a self-signup trial on Redwood and are interested in evaluating Dedicated capacity for production. Our immediate need is to validate that we can sustain a steady 150-220 QPS for short bursts (avg ~180 QPS) with an average prompt+response token count of ~75 tokens and a P95 latency target under 120ms for the model family we're testing.

A few quick facts:
- Workload: conversational assistant for clinical triage (sensitive, low-latency requirement)
- Peak concurrency: ~300 concurrent users, but most traffic is short bursts
- Preferred model: open-llm-fam-3 (we tested quantized variant locally)

I've attached a small sample of our synthetic request traces (sample_workload.csv) and can share more telemetry if helpful. We're hoping to book a dedicated-capacity technical demo to see an apples-to-apples run and confirm cost/latency tradeoffs and fallback behavior (canary to hosted).

What availability do you have for a short planning call this week? Also curious if you can walk through your recommended fallback/canary routing for Dedicated.

Thanks,
Alex Shepard
Head of Platform Integrations
SpectraHealth

Attachment: sample_workload.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

Couple technical clarifications from my side:

- Sequence length distribution matters more than mean. If >5% of requests are >512 tokens we need to account for that in batching and memory planning.
- For 180 QPS sustained with short (<=100 token) responses, the main levers are: continuous batching window, per-GPU batch cap, and KV cache affinity. We'll pre-config a quantization profile that worked in earlier tests for open-llm-fam-3.
- Canary fallback: we should demonstrate request-level routing and graceful throttling; important to show observed tail latencies when hosted capacity is hit.

I'll prepare a short latency-KPI matrix and a baseline run script. If Ben can do Wed 09:00 PT dry run internally I'll sync after the run and then we can propose slots to the customer.

-Mina
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
